title: Machine-learning-guided synthesis confirms superconductivity in Mo20Re6Si4
summary: Researchers used a deep-learning composition model to prioritize a sigma-phase ternary compound, synthesized Mo20Re6Si4, and measured bulk superconductivity with a critical temperature of 5.4 K. Magnetic susceptibility and a specific-heat anomaly support the bulk transition. The paper reports mixed model performance on its small test set and describes the model as guidance alongside chemical intuition.
ai_technology: Deep-learning neural network that classifies compositions as superconducting and predicts critical temperature
organization: Rutgers University; Flatiron Institute; University of South Carolina; Princeton University; Michigan State University

evidence.tested: Researchers used a deep-learning composition model to prioritize a sigma-phase ternary compound, synthesized Mo20Re6Si4, and measured bulk superconductivity with a critical temperature of 5.4 K.
evidence.unknown: The result is experimental and supported by bulk measurements, but the preprint reports a small, specialized evaluation set and mixed predictor performance. Chemical intuition also guided candidate selection; AI's contribution was a search hint, not independent autonomous discovery. The compound is a materials-physics finding rather than a new general superconducting mechanism.
evidence.ai_role: Provided composition-based hints that helped researchers select Mo20Re6Si4 for synthesis; laboratory resistivity, magnetic-susceptibility and specific-heat measurements established the superconducting result.
